common_name: Wildeve Rose (Deep Pink David Austin Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall in full sun with good air circulation; Wildeve, named after a character in Thomas Hardy's The Return of the Native, bears deep pink cupped blooms.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil enriched with compost. Named after a character from Thomas Hardy's novel The Return of the Native, Wildeve bears rich, deep pink, cupped double blooms with a strong, fruity fragrance, opening on a compact, well-branched shrub that fits smaller beds and mixed borders. Its saturated color reads boldly from a distance and pairs well with softer pastel companions. It reblooms reliably from late spring through fall; prune canes back by about a third in late winter to encourage strong new flowering wood, and deadhead spent blooms through the season to sustain continued flowering.
sources: American Rose Society — English rose archive

Its classic pink coloring and shapely flower form give it broad appeal as a reliable, easy-to-place English rose. It reblooms in flushes from late spring through fall; prune canes back by about a third in late winter to encourage strong new flowering wood, and deadhead spent blooms through the season to sustain continued flowering.
